questions.question: Why was the original decision about the acoustic treatment for the fourth-floor refit changed?
questions.answer_text: Before: recycled PET felt wall panels from Tessaline across all 310 square metres of the floor, because Dmitri argues the panels reach the 0.85 absorption target at 62 pounds per square metre, about 20 percent under the timber slat quote, and count toward the landlord's recycled-content clause. Triggered by: Fatima (evidence): Fatima reports that the insurer's surveyor says escape-corridor linings must reach Euroclass B-s1,d0, while the Tessaline test certificate shows only C-s2,d0. Kwame (challenge): Kwame objects that signing the order as it stands could void the building cover, with installation booked for 3 February. Ravi (reconsideration): Ravi reopens the panel order now that the supplier has replied about the corridor rating. After: Tessaline PET felt panels everywhere except the 46 square metres of escape corridor, which get the mineral-wool-core version rated B-s1,d0, adding 3,800 pounds, because Henrik argues for keeping the felt everywhere else and switching only the 46 square metres of corridor to Tessaline's mineral-wool-core panel rated B-s1,d0, which adds 3,800 pounds and keeps the 3 February date.
